## 10. The dossier and the mini-dossier (schema decided Sat 17:41)

One schema for both. The **dossier** is built offline for each of the 46 detailed suppliers. The
**case overlay** is added at session open from the case file and the opening e-mails; for a
supplier we have no data on it is the whole dossier (the mini-dossier). Fixed now so A and B build
against the same thing. A better data point found later costs little: add the field, run the
builder again.

**Change rule.** Fields marked `*` are read by code (calculator, argument bank): their names and
meaning are frozen for `schema_version` 1. Any field may be added at any time. Renaming or removing
a `*` field needs a `schema_version` bump and a `[decision]` in the log.

**Interface** (`sellm/intel.py`):

- `uv run python -m sellm.intel build` writes `sellm/dossiers/<supplier number>.json` for every
  detailed supplier plus `index.json`. Deterministic (sorted keys, no LLM, no network), under 10 s,
  **committed**, so the final machine needs no rebuild. Rebuild and commit after the Sunday release.
- `dossier(supplier_id, part_ids, case=None, opening=None, package=None) -> dict`: the stored
  dossier restricted to `part_ids` (parts it does not supply are built live from the package), with
  the case overlay merged in. `opening` is the threads dict as in `decide(case, threads)` (a thread
  may be a list or `{"messages": [...]}`); `package` a DataPackage or its path, default
  `$ARENA_DATA`. Never raises; for an unknown supplier it returns the overlay alone
  (`coverage: "case_only"`). A blocked old vendor record whose company lives on under a detailed
  record of the same name is mapped to it (in the data: `sup:71999` -> `sup:70210`), with a warning.
  About 1 ms per call once the package is loaded (the first call loads it, about 0.1 s).
- `citable` is filled by `sellm.claims.citable_for(package, supplier_id, part_ids)` (group C); the
  builder and the overlay call it. `arguments(case, supplier_id, dossier)` (group C) turns it into
  sentences for the negotiator.
- Units as in the data: prices per the part's `price_unit`; yearly rates as fractions (0.09);
  percentages as numbers (9.5).

**Fields** (`*` = read by code, frozen)

| Field | Content | Source |
|---|---|---|
| `schema_version`*, `supplier_id`*, `coverage`* | `1`; `sup:...`; `full` (detailed supplier), `thin` (vendor master and spend only), `case_only` | |
| `built_from` | package version, Sunday release merged, case ID of the overlay | |
| `identity` | name, country, category, legal_form, founded, owner_type, group_parent, staff, turnover_eur (or band), equity_ratio_pct, credit_index now and 12 months ago, vda63_grade, abc_class, supplier_since | `suppliers`, `supplier_intel` |
| `standard_terms`* | payment_days, skonto_days, skonto_pct, incoterm, lead_time_days | `suppliers`; in a case the quote PDF wins |
| `economics.cost_of_money`* | its yearly cost of money, and `cost_of_money_basis` (text) | rule below |
| `economics.cash_pressure`* | `low`, `medium`, `high` | rule below |
| `economics.archetype`* | `family`, `group`, `job_shop`, `monopolist`, `trader`, `other` (the lab's names) | rule below |
| `economics.our_share_of_turnover_pct` | our spend in the last fiscal year / its turnover: how much it needs us | `spend_cube`, `supplier_intel` |
| `economics.our_spend_eur` | per fiscal year | `spend_cube` |
| `economics.we_pay_late_days` | mean days we paid after the due date (paying on time is a cheap gift) | `invoices` |
| `signals`* | list of `{kind, strength 1-3, evidence: [IDs], excerpt}`, `kind` from the table below | documents, news (not `noise`), quote remarks, history notes; in a case also briefing, trigger doc, quote e-mail and PDF remarks |
| `contract` | id, valid_to, notice_days, price_basis, payment_days, incoterm, index clauses `{id, series, material_share, deadband_pct}` | `contracts`, `contract_clauses` |
| `parts.<part>` | description, category, material_group, uom, `price_unit`*, quota_pct, tooling_owner, planned_lead_time_days | `parts`, `sourcing` |
| `parts.<part>.current_price`* | price, valid_from | `price_conditions` |
| `parts.<part>.history` | per event: date, type, asked_pct, settled_pct, note; plus `mean_give_pct` (asked minus settled) and `below_full_cost` | `negotiation_history` |

| `parts.<part>.drivers` | per cost-driver series: weight, last month, change over 6 and 12 months, the two `idx:` IDs of each window | `cost_drivers`, `index_values` |

| `documents` | id, date, kind, subject, author, full text | `documents`, `correspondence/` |

| `stated_drivers` (added, overlay) | each "<series> rose x % in twelve months and is y % of our cost" in the opening e-mail: `{series, direction, stated_change_pct, cost_share_pct, true_change_12m_pct, ids_12m, matches}` (matches: within 0.5 points of the index) | opening e-mail, `facts.json` |
| `opening_offer` (added, overlay) | `{offer_id, terms, stated, standard, fixed, validity_days, missing_fields}` from the first term sheet and the quote PDF | opening e-mail |
| `case_facts` (added, overlay) | the case's own `facts`, as a dict by ID (a list is converted) | case file |
| `warnings` (added) | what could not be read or built; empty normally | |

**Rules for the derived fields.** Initial rules; calibrate them in the lab and change them only in
the builder.

- `should_cost`: the row whose `supplier_id` is this supplier (`cost:310012-70110` for Brandlhuber,
  not `cost:310012`, which is Wimbacher's plant); else the generic row without a supplier. Another
  supplier's plant estimate is never this supplier's should-cost and is not cited to it.
- `floor_estimate`: plant-specific should-cost, value = unit_cost, band = its `confidence_pct`
  (floors came out within 3-5 % of it, `docs/LEARNINGS.md`); generic German should-cost times the
  country factor (AT, CH 1.05; CZ, PL, HU 0.825; TR 0.75; CN 0.7), band 15 %; none: null, and the
  calculator falls back to a share of the opening.
- `cost_of_money`: with skonto terms, `skonto_pct / 100 * 360 / (payment_days - skonto_days)` (2 %
  at 10 days instead of 30 is 0.36); else archetype `job_shop` or `cash_short` strength 2 or more:
  0.25 (P05's Czech job shop measured about 0.35); else group 0.065 (P02, P08), family 0.09 (D01),
  founder or private 0.10; plus 0.05 if the credit index is 300 or more or rose 20 points or more in
  12 months. The skonto rate is measured, so it gets no surcharge (calibrated Sat 18:30).
  The credit index is higher-is-worse (groups 147-178; the two cash-short skonto suppliers rose to 302
  and 343).
- `cash_pressure`: `high` with skonto terms or `cash_short` strength 2 or more; `medium` with an
  equity ratio under 25 %, a credit index of 250 or more, or a rising credit index; else `low`.
- `archetype`: `group` if the owner type is group; else `job_shop` if staff < 80 or cash pressure is
  high; else `family` if family-owned; else `trader` for raw material or a quote remark "supply from
  stock"; `monopolist` overrides when
  `capacity_tight` or `list_price_fixed` is signalled and the part has no alternative; else `other`.
- `citable`: only what the arena accepts (an `idx` pair is one series, at most 12 months apart,
  ending within the last 12 months of the data). Every entry is checked with `sellm/lab/claims.py`
  at build time: 0 `contradicted`. Facts that help the supplier (a rising index) stay in with
  `helps_buyer: false`, so A knows what the supplier may cite.

**Signal kinds** (`signals[].kind`, frozen vocabulary: add kinds, do not rename). Strength is
min(3, distinct pieces of evidence): one per text, one per structured condition; a news item found by
its topic and by its words counts once. Noise news and market news never count. Rules and patterns:
`sellm/intel/signals.py` (calibrated Sat 18:30 against all 46 suppliers' texts).

| Kind | Evidence in the data | What it means for us |
|---|---|---|
| `cash_short` | "Could you pay our invoices within 10 days?", liquidity, "the bank", skonto terms, quote remark "Payment within 10 days requested", news `credit_downgrade`, `credit_watch`, `short_time_work`. A low equity ratio is not evidence here; it raises `cash_pressure` to `medium` | trade faster payment for price; it values payment days at its high cost of money; do not squeeze its margin |
| `wants_volume` | "focus on customers with volume", idle shop floor, news `free_capacity`, "accepted below full cost to keep the volume" | a longer contract, full-need coverage or a bundle buys price |
| `capacity_tight` | news `allocation`, `full_order_book`, `big_order`, `chip_shortage` | secure volume and lead time first; price moves little |
| `list_price_fixed` | "head-office directive", "list conditions" in quote remarks; "no room on price this year: head office has frozen all price reductions" | do not fight the list price; move payment, start date, freight, chargeback |
| `material_hedged` | "material covered until ..." | index arguments are weak until then; ask for a later start or a fixed price |
| `partnership` | past favours and the reciprocity asked for ("kept supplying at the old price ... expects partnership in return"), "long-standing", "for generations". Read from the text, not the subject: "Visit by the owner" notes are often about something else, and the vendor-master date is 1996-01-01 for 36 of 46 suppliers | appreciation and reciprocity; never an ultimatum |
| `margin_floor` | "cannot sign anything that lowers our margin"; a part priced at or below its plant-specific should-cost (e.g. Wimbacher 310012 at 0.97) | the price is near its floor; trade terms, not price |
| `quality_problem` | latest scorecard amber or red, ppm above 1,500, an overdue 8D (each condition counts once), 8D/complaint/defect in its texts | lever for ppm commitment and chargeback; cite `sc` and `qn` |
| `delivery_problem` | latest on-time delivery below 75 % (9 of 46; below the 95 % target are 43 of 46, which says nothing); strength 2 below 65 %, 3 below 55 % | cite OTD; ask for a lead-time commitment |
| `ownership_change` | news `new_owner`, `succession`, `restructuring`, `refocus` | new decision makers, risk that it walks; be clear and fair |
| `approval_ladder` | owner type group or a group parent, "head office", "price changes above 2 % need the approval of their pricing committee" | expect a round on hold before a bigger move; be patient |
| `price_claim` | a letter with `asked_pct` and stated reasons; in the opening e-mail "<series> rose x % in twelve months and is y % of our cost" | check each stated cost driver against its index; cite the ones that fell |
| `informal_costing` (added Sat 18:30) | "works from his own spreadsheet, last updated two years ago", "had not followed his material and energy prices closely since the 2022 peak; his office manager does the costing" | the supplier does not track its own costs: one verified index figure can disarm it ("we didn't know that"); bring exactly one strong figure |

**The case overlay** (mini-dossier): at session open, before the first move, under 100 ms, no LLM.

- `identity` from the vendor master if the ID is known (also the about 400 suppliers known only by
  name, category and spend), else the name from the opening e-mail.
- `standard_terms` from the quote PDF (`arena_kit.docs.standard_terms`), overriding stored values.
- `signals` from the briefing, the trigger doc, the quote e-mail and PDF remarks, and any `doc:` or
  `news:` in the case's `facts`.
- `citable` from the case's `facts` (a dict keyed by ID like `facts.json`, as the Calculator already
  reads it; accept a list too) and its `refs`.
- `should_cost` and `floor_estimate` from a `cost:` fact of the case.
- `alternatives` from `buyer.alternative` and, in an RFQ, the other suppliers' offers (their
  `offer:` IDs are citable in the session).
- Merge: lists are united by ID; scalar values from the case win.
- `alternatives` entries from the case carry a `kind`: `buyer_alternative` (our alternative quote,
  marked on the existing entry if the quote is already listed), `current_contract`, `rfq_rival`

"""Build every detailed supplier's dossier and write them to sellm/dossiers/ (docs/PLAN.md section 10)."""

from pathlib import Path

from . import assemble, render, signals
from .extract import Source, number
from .schema import SCHEMA_VERSION
from .serialize import write

DOSSIERS = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent / "dossiers"


def citable_hook():
    """Group C's sellm.claims.citable_for, once it exists; until then the dossiers carry no citable facts."""
    try:
        from sellm.claims import citable_for
    except ImportError:
        return None
    return citable_for


def build_one(src, sid):
    d = assemble.build_supplier(src, sid)
    signals.apply(d)
    hook = citable_hook()
    if hook:
        try:

# Get the team's latest commits and push ours: pull --rebase, then push. Safe to run any time.
# Usage: scripts/sync
set -uo pipefail
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." || exit 1
branch=$(git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD)
for attempt in 1 2 3; do
  if ! git pull --rebase --autostash --quiet origin "$branch"; then
    echo "sync: pull --rebase stopped (conflict or no network)." >&2
    echo "sync: on a conflict fix the files, 'git add' them, 'git rebase --continue', then run scripts/sync again." >&2
    exit 1
  fi
  if [ "$(git rev-list --count "origin/$branch..HEAD")" = "0" ]; then
    echo "sync: up to date with origin/$branch at $(git rev-parse --short HEAD)"
    exit 0
  fi
  if git push --quiet origin "$branch"; then
    echo "sync: pushed, origin/$branch is at $(git rev-parse --short HEAD)"
    exit 0
  fi
  echo "sync: push rejected (someone pushed first?), retrying ($attempt/3)" >&2
  sleep 2
done
echo "sync: could not push after 3 attempts - check the network and your access to the repo" >&2
exit 1

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Pre-flight for the Live Final on the machine that runs it (docs/CONTEXT.md section 12; macOS and Linux,
# bash 3.2). Checks everything the final needs, plays one free sandbox case through the final runner and
# prints the command that starts the final. Nothing here waits for input.
# Usage: scripts/preflight            all checks (about 3 min)
#        scripts/preflight --quick    skip the full test suite and the sandbox case (about 30 s)
#        scripts/preflight --no-sync  do not pull (after the freeze: the final runs the checked-out commit)
set -uo pipefail
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." || exit 1
quick=no
sync=yes
for a in "$@"; do
  case "$a" in
    --quick) quick=yes ;;
    --no-sync) sync=no ;;
    *) echo "preflight: unknown option $a" >&2; exit 2 ;;
  esac
done
fails=0
warns=0
ok() { printf '  ok    %s\n' "$1"; }
warn() { printf '  WARN  %s\n' "$1"; warns=$((warns + 1)); }
fail() { printf '  FAIL  %s\n' "$1"; fails=$((fails + 1)); }
step() { printf '\n%s\n' "$1"; }
now() { TZ=Europe/Berlin date '+%a %H:%M'; }

echo "preflight: $(now) CEST on $(hostname) ($(uname -s))"

step "1. Repo"
if [ "$sync" = yes ]; then
  if scripts/sync >/dev/null 2>&1; then ok "scripts/sync: in step with origin"; else fail "scripts/sync failed (network? conflict?)"; fi
fi
branch=$(git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD)
[ "$branch" = main ] && ok "branch main" || fail "branch is $branch, not main"
if [ -z "$(git status --porcelain --untracked-files=no)" ]; then ok "no local changes to tracked files"; else warn "local changes to tracked files (git status): the final runs what is on disk"; fi
ok "commit $(git rev-parse HEAD) (this hash goes into the submission)"

step "2. Tools and environment"
command -v uv >/dev/null 2>&1 && ok "uv $(uv --version 2>/dev/null | cut -d' ' -f2)" || fail "uv not found (https://docs.astral.sh/uv/)"
if uv sync --all-extras --quiet >/dev/null 2>&1; then ok "uv sync --all-extras"; else fail "uv sync --all-extras failed"; fi
if [ -f .env ]; then
  ok ".env present"
  for key in ARENA_URL ARENA_API_KEY; do
    if grep -Eq "^[[:space:]]*$key=.+" .env || [ -n "${!key:-}" ]; then ok "$key set"; else fail "$key missing in .env"; fi
  done
  if grep -Eq '^[[:space:]]*LLM_PROVIDER=.+' .env; then
    ok "LLM settings present (only needed for --agent llm or an LLM writer)"
  fi
else
  fail ".env missing: cp .env.example .env and put in the team key (never commit it)"
fi

step "3. Data (the Sunday release is public from Sun 08:00)"
if uv run arena data >/tmp/preflight-data.$$ 2>&1; then
  ok "uv run arena data: $(tr '\n' ' ' </tmp/preflight-data.$$)"
else
  fail "uv run arena data failed: $(tail -1 /tmp/preflight-data.$$)"
fi
rm -f /tmp/preflight-data.$$
[ -f data/package/facts.json ] && ok "data/package unpacked" || fail "data/package/facts.json missing"
if [ -f data/release-sunday/facts.json ]; then
  ok "Sunday release unpacked (DataPackage merges it)"
elif [ "$(TZ=Europe/Berlin date +%u%H)" -ge 708 ] 2>/dev/null; then
  fail "Sunday release missing after 08:00: run uv run arena data again"
else
  warn "Sunday release not public yet (from Sun 08:00): run this again after 08:00"
fi

step "4. Arena"
me=$(uv run arena me 2>&1)
if printf '%s' "$me" | grep -q '"status": "active"'; then
  left=$(printf '%s' "$me" | sed -n 's/.*"left": \([0-9]*\).*/\1/p' | head -1)
  ok "uv run arena me: team active, practice sessions left ${left:-?}"
  [ -n "$left" ] && [ "$left" -lt 15 ] && warn "few practice sessions left ($left): keep 10 for the rehearsal"
else
  fail "uv run arena me: $(printf '%s' "$me" | tail -1)"
fi

step "5. Rules (docs/CONTEXT.md section 11)"
hits=$(grep -nE '/v1/events|events/stream|/v1/screen|"/screen|leaderboard|/v1/results|"/results' \
  sellm/*.py sellm/intel/*.py 2>/dev/null | grep -vE '^\S+:[0-9]+:\s*#' | grep -v 'never the live feed' || true)
if [ -z "$hits" ]; then ok "no live-feed endpoint in the agent's code path (sellm/, sellm/intel/)"; else fail "live-feed endpoint in the agent's code: $hits"; fi
if git ls-files | grep -qE '(^|/)\.env$'; then fail ".env is tracked by git"; else ok ".env not in git"; fi

step "6. Tests"
if uv run ruff check . >/dev/null 2>&1; then ok "ruff check"; else fail "ruff check (uv run ruff check .)"; fi
if [ "$quick" = yes ]; then
  if uv run pytest -q tests/test_runner.py tests/test_claims.py >/tmp/preflight-tests.$$ 2>&1; then
    ok "runner and claims tests: $(tail -1 /tmp/preflight-tests.$$)"
  else
    fail "runner and claims tests: $(tail -1 /tmp/preflight-tests.$$)"
  fi
else
  if uv run pytest -q >/tmp/preflight-tests.$$ 2>&1; then ok "pytest: $(tail -1 /tmp/preflight-tests.$$)"; else fail "pytest: $(tail -1 /tmp/preflight-tests.$$)"; fi
fi
rm -f /tmp/preflight-tests.$$

if [ "$quick" = no ]; then
  step "7. One free sandbox case through the final runner (no quota)"
  out=$(ARENA_NO_PULL=1 uv run python -m sellm.runner --set sandbox --agent sellm --cases D01 2>&1)
  done_line=$(printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep 'done:' | tail -1)
  if printf '%s' "$done_line" | grep -q 'crashes 0'; then
    ok "sandbox D01: ${done_line#*done: }"
  else
    fail "sandbox D01 through the runner: $(printf '%s\n' "$out" | tail -3 | tr '\n' ' ')"
  fi
fi

step "8. Machine"
if [ "$(uname -s)" = Darwin ]; then
  if pmset -g batt 2>/dev/null | grep -q "AC Power"; then ok "on AC power"; else warn "on battery: plug the laptop in"; fi
  if pgrep -x caffeinate >/dev/null 2>&1; then ok "caffeinate is running"; else warn "no caffeinate: run 'caffeinate -dims &' so the Mac does not sleep"; fi
else
  ok "Linux: make sure the machine does not suspend (systemd-inhibit or the power settings)"
fi
if curl -s -m 10 -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' https://arena.tacto.ai/health 2>/dev/null | grep -q 200; then
  ok "arena.tacto.ai reachable"
else
  fail "arena.tacto.ai/health not reachable (network?)"
fi

echo
echo "preflight: $fails failed, $warns warnings ($(now) CEST)"
cat <<'EOF'

Start the final (Sun 11:30 at the latest, it polls until wave 1 opens and stops after wave 5):
  caffeinate -dims &      # macOS: no sleep
  nohup uv run python -m sellm.runner --set final --agent sellm > runs/logs/final.out 2>&1 &
  tail -f runs/logs/final.out      # watch; the per-move log is runs/logs/<time>-runner-final.log
After a crash: run the same command again; it resumes the running sessions.
EOF
[ "$fails" -eq 0 ]

`play()` sends one message and waits for the reply while the other threads' 60-second clocks run.

Across 12 threads: 8 claims `verified`, 8 `duplicate`, 0 `contradicted`. Three cases had none at

```bash
cp .env.example .env     # set ARENA_API_KEY and the LLM: LLM_PROVIDER=openai, LLM_MODEL=gpt-6-sol, LLM_API_KEY
uv sync --all-extras
uv run arena data        # unpacks data/package (gitignored)
uv run arena me          # team + practice quota
uv run arena play case:D01 --agent sellm -v               # sandbox: free, real supplier bots
uv run arena play case:P01 --agent llm -v
uv run arena run --set final --agent llm --parallel 10   # Live Final, start before 12:00
```

Agents: `naive` and `llm` are the kit's examples; `llm` is the baseline to beat (61.5 on the 10
hosted cases). `sellm` is ours: `sellm/agent.py`, for now the lab's numbers-only Calculator. The
final command switches to `--agent sellm` only once it beats `llm`.
input.new_string:
```bash
cp .env.example .env     # set ARENA_URL, ARENA_API_KEY, ARENA_DATA=data/package; for an LLM agent also
                         # LLM_PROVIDER=openai, LLM_MODEL, LLM_API_KEY (values never in git)
uv sync --all-extras
uv run arena data        # unpacks data/package (and data/release-sunday from Sun 08:00; gitignored)
uv run arena me          # team + practice quota
scripts/preflight        # everything the final needs, plus one free sandbox case through the runner
```

The Live Final runs through our runner, `sellm/runner.py` (start it before 12:00; it polls until wave 1
opens, plays every case of a wave in parallel, closes each case before the wave's cap and stops after
wave 5; run the same command again after a crash and it resumes the running sessions):

```bash
nohup uv run python -m sellm.runner --set final --agent sellm > runs/logs/final.out 2>&1 &
```

Measured runs use the same runner: `uv run python -m sellm.runner --set sandbox --cases D01 D02
--repeat 3` (free) or `--set practice --cases P01 P05` (quota). Logs: `runs/logs/<time>-runner-<set>.log`
(every move) and `.jsonl` (one row per case). `uv run arena play case:D01 --agent sellm -v` plays one case
with the kit's runner.

Agents (`--agent`): `sellm` is ours (`sellm/agent.py` -> `sellm/negotiator.py`: the price path and the
term sheets from code, data arguments from `sellm/claims.py`, supplier dossiers from `sellm/intel/`);
`naive` and `llm` are the kit's examples (`llm` scored 61.5 on the 10 hosted cases). Which one the
final runs is decided in `docs/STATUS.md`.

- **Final-Runner `sellm/runner.py`**:

  - Er spielt die 5 Wellen, schließt jeden Fall vor dem Zeitlimit der Welle und setzt nach einem Absturz die laufenden Sessions fort.

Gleichzeitige Mails an mehrere Lieferanten bremsen sich bei der Arena also gegenseitig aus.

Als Nächstes würde ich eine Option einbauen, bei der pro Session nur eine Mail gleichzeitig unterwegs ist, und sie mit einer Session auf P05 testen. Bis dahin ist offen, welcher Runner im Finale die Fälle mit mehreren Lieferanten spielt. Die Übergabe für das Team mit den nächsten Schritten steht im Log (`[handoff]` Sat 21:25).

**Was das Team entscheiden muss:** ob das Finale mit `--agent sellm` läuft. Jonathans v1.2 kam auf 67.5 gegenüber 61.5 der Baseline.

**Zuerst: Wir sind nicht schlechter geworden**
- Mein voller Lauf mit 52.2 lief noch mit dem alten Negotiator v1.1. Er ist in 9 von 10 Fällen identisch mit Jonathans altem Lauf (53.2).
- Jonathans v1.2 von 21:06 kam auf **67.5**. Die Kit-Baseline liegt bei 61.5.

**Warum „pro Fall die perfekte Taktik“ riskant ist**
- **Das Finale spielt andere Fälle.** Die Fälle sind versteckt, die Lieferanten neu, und bis zu ein Drittel kombiniert Typen, die das Training nie zeigt. Eine Taktik, die P04 auswendig kennt, nützt bei einem fremden Lieferanten nichts.
- **Das Lab ist optimistisch.** Die im Lab beste Taktik kam dort auf etwa 0.90 und real auf 0.79. Ein Lab-Wert von 0.9–1 heißt real eher 0.75–0.85.
- **0.9–1 ist nicht überall erreichbar.** Bei P02, P08 und P18 hat in keinem Lauf irgendein Agent auch nur die Hälfte geschafft.

**Wie ich es machen würde**
1. **Persönlichkeit nach Lieferantentyp statt nach Fall**, etwa 5 bis 7 Spielbücher:
   - knapp bei Kasse: Zahlungsziel gegen Preis
   - Listenpreis eingefroren: auf andere Bedingungen ausweichen
   - Konzern mit Freigabe-Hierarchie: Geduld
   - Familienbetrieb: Wertschätzung, kein Ultimatum
   - Rohmaterial mit Index-Klausel
   - Qualitätsfall
   - Engpass-Lieferant
   - RFQ mit mehreren Bietern

   Die Signale dafür stehen schon in Omars Dossiers, auch für Lieferanten, die wir nicht kennen.
2. **Auswahl per Regeln mit Confidence.** Eine Persönlichkeit wird nur gewählt, wenn die Signale klar sind. Sonst spielt v1.2 als sicherer Standard. Alle Persönlichkeiten zu einem Durchschnitt zusammenzufassen wäre falsch, dann geht der Vorteil verloren.

Das wird billig: Die Practice-Lieferanten antworten auf gleiche Mails exakt gleich, also reicht bei Einzelfällen eine Session pro Variante für einen fairen Vergleich.

**Eine Sache hat aus meiner Sicht Vorrang.** Mein offener Runner-Punkt: Bei RFQ-Fällen hat der Kit-Runner auf P05 0.769 geholt, unserer 0.665. Jeder Fall zählt gleich, deshalb würde ich das zuerst klären. Danach würde ich die Persönlichkeiten mit einem Zeitlimit bis etwa 01:00 bauen.

result.output:
# The lab: test buyer strategies without spending practice quota

A local copy of the arena with simulated suppliers. Any agent with `decide(case, threads)` plays
against it exactly as against the arena (the kit's `RemoteTable` interface), for free, a few hundred
negotiations per second on a laptop. No arena calls, no LLM calls unless you choose the `llm` agent.

**What it is good for:** ranking strategy variants by their mean over many scenarios; finding the
mistakes that cost points in the final (crashes, refused moves, broken must-haves, deals worse than
the opening, timeouts in RFQs, running out of time). **What it is not:** a prediction of one case's
score. A lab winner is a hypothesis until the sandbox (`case:D01`, `case:D02`, free) or one practice
case confirms it.

## The UI

`scripts/lab ui` starts a small local server in the background (if it is not running yet) and opens
http://127.0.0.1:8765 - nobody else can reach it. The page only works while that server runs;
`scripts/lab ui-stop` ends it (runs it started keep going).

- **Start**: search, compare or stress with every option as a form field; knobs as JSON or a table,
  or loaded from any earlier run's `best.json` (rank N). Runs go to the background and keep going
  when the UI is closed.
- **Runs**: every run with live progress and the rendered report; stop a running one; **extend**
  (refills the form with more minutes, seeds and scenarios); **use #1 knobs** for a compare;
  **stress-test #1**; **#1 as sellm/agent.py KNOBS** (a block to paste into `sellm/agent.py`); export
  `report.md`, `best.json`, `rows.csv` (one row per negotiation, for a spreadsheet) or the whole run as a zip.
- **Play one**: any twin or generated scenario with any agent and knobs, the full transcript.

## Quick start

```bash
scripts/lab play P01                  # one negotiation against the P01 twin, every e-mail printed
scripts/lab play X01-007 naive        # a generated scenario, the kit's naive agent
scripts/lab compare naive calc        # agents side by side (background, ~1 min)
scripts/lab search 60                 # a 60-minute search for the best Calculator knobs (background)
scripts/lab stress calc               # stress test: everything the final may bring (background)
scripts/lab status                    # what is running, newest progress, where the report is
scripts/lab stop                      # stop a run
```

Every run writes `runs/lab/<time>-<command>[-label]/`: `report.md` (read this), `best.json` (the ten
best variants with their knobs), `progress.log` (live). Raw rows and scenarios are git-ignored.
Commit `report.md` and `best.json` of runs that matter and log them as `[run]` (AGENTS.md).

Use a result: `--knobs runs/lab/<run>/best.json` (rank 1) or `...best.json#3` (rank 3), e.g.
`scripts/lab stress calc --knobs runs/lab/<run>/best.json`. Your own agent: `--agent module:Class`
(constructed with the data package if it takes one), e.g. `scripts/lab compare calc sellm.agent:SellmAgent`.

## Options (all commands that play)

| Option | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `--mode parallel\|sequential` | parallel | one loop per thread (what our final runner must do) / the kit's `play()` (one thread at a time; RFQ threads time out) |
| `--no-clock` | off | no simulated time: no timeouts, no wave cap |
| `--wave-cap S` | 480 | seconds per case, as a Live Final wave; the runner closes 90 s before it with the kit's `closing_move` |
| `--think S` | 2.0 | our seconds per move; `-1` = the real time the agent took (use for LLM agents) |
| `--fixed-twins` | off | the fitted twins only; by default each run draws a member of each twin's family |
| `--supplier engine\|llm` | engine | who plays the suppliers: the calibrated rules, or an LLM inside them (costs tokens) |
| `--invented N`, `--test N` | 160, 80 | generated scenarios for training and for the unseen test |
| `--seeds N` | 2 | runs per strategy and scenario |

## Reading a report

- Rank by **Test**: scenarios the search never tuned on (held-out twins P04, P10, P18 plus fresh
  generated ones). A big gap between Train and Test means the variant is fitted to the lab, not good.
- **Crash, 422, Broken, Worse** must be 0 for anything we run in the final. **Below alt**: ended
  under what walking away would have scored. **Wave cap**: ran out of time. **Timeouts**: threads
  left more than 60 s.
- The tables below the ranking break the winner down by case type, goal, supplier archetype and edge
  case: that is where to look for the next improvement.

## Two kinds of supplier: engine and LLM

"""Play strategies against the lab's suppliers, rank them, and show where they are weak.

Scenario pools (built once per run in the main process, saved as `scenarios.json.gz`, loaded by every
worker):
- **train**: the twins except the held-out ones (P04, P10, P18, docs/PLAN.md section 8), plus
  generated scenarios (unplayed case files and invented ones, `invent.py`).
- **test**: the held-out twins plus freshly generated scenarios from another seed. A search never
  looks at them; its best variants are scored on them at the end, so the report shows how much of
  a gain survives on cases it was not tuned on.

Modes:
- `compare`: named strategies on train and test.
- `search`: random variants of the `Calculator` knobs, successive halving (many variants on few
  scenarios, the better half on twice as many), then mutations of the best, until the time is up -
  checked between batches, not only between rounds - then the test phase.

Every negotiation runs with the clock and the wave cap (`play_lab`), sequentially as the kit's
runner or with one loop per thread, and twins vary within their families. Progress goes to
`progress.log` in the run folder as it happens.
"""

import importlib
import json
import math
import os
import random
import statistics
import time
import traceback
from concurrent.futures import ProcessPoolExecutor
from pathlib import Path

from . import invent, store, twins
from .spaces import sample, space_for
from .strategies import registry

HOLDOUT = {"P04", "P10", "P18"}
BATCH = 400  # negotiations between two looks at the clock
_W = {}  # per worker process


def build_pools(n_invented, invent_seed, n_test, package):
    tw = twins.load()
    train = [s for s in tw if s.name not in HOLDOUT] + invent.generate(n_invented, package, seed=invent_seed)
    test = [s for s in tw if s.name in HOLDOUT] + invent.generate(n_test, package, seed=invent_seed + 1000)
    return train, test


def reader_for(opts):
    """None (keyword rules) or an LLM reader of our e-mails, cached per text."""
    if opts.get("reader") != "llm":
        return None
    from arena_kit.agents.llm import llm_from_env

    from .reader import llm_reader

    model = os.environ.get("LAB_READER_MODEL")
    if model:
        os.environ["LLM_MODEL"] = model
    return llm_reader(llm_from_env())


def _init(path, opts):
    from arena_kit.cli import load_env
    from arena_kit.data import DataPackage

    load_env()
    pkg = DataPackage(os.environ.get("ARENA_DATA", "data/package"))
    pkg.lookup("")
    _W.update(pkg=pkg, scenarios={s.name: s for s in store.load(path)}, opts=opts, reader=reader_for(opts))
    _W["brain"] = brain_for(opts)


def brain_for(opts):
    """The LLM that plays the suppliers when opts['supplier'] == 'llm', else None."""
    if opts.get("supplier") != "llm":
        return None
    from .llm_supplier import Brain

    return Brain(cache=not opts.get("no_cache"))


def make_agent(name, knobs, package):
    """A strategy by name: naive, calc, llm, or any importable 'module:Class' (built with the data
    package if its constructor takes one, then the knobs)."""
    if ":" in name:
        module, cls = name.split(":", 1)
        klass = getattr(importlib.import_module(module), cls)
        if knobs:  # an agent that takes no knobs fails loudly rather than ignoring them
            return klass(package, **knobs)
        try:
            return klass(package)
        except TypeError:
            return klass()
    return registry(package)[name](**(knobs or {}))


def _alt_score(s):
    from arena_kit.cost import score

    return score(s.c_open, s.c_alt, s.c_best) if s.c_alt else 0.0


def _play(job):
    """One negotiation: (strategy name, knobs, scenario name, seed) -> a result row."""
    name, knobs, scen_name, seed = job
    s, o = _W["scenarios"][scen_name], _W["opts"]
    row = {
        "strategy": name,
        "knobs": knobs,
        "scenario": scen_name,
        "kind": s.kind,
        "seed": seed,
        "type": s.case.get("type"),
        "goal": s.case["buyer"].get("category_goal"),

    return name + (" " + json.dumps(knobs, sort_keys=True) if knobs else "")


def compare(run, names, seeds=2, knobs=None):
    knobs = knobs or {}
    jobs = [(n, knobs.get(n, {}), s.name, k) for n in names for s in run.train + run.test for k in range(seeds)]
    run.log(f"compare {names}: {len(jobs)} negotiations")
    t0 = time.time()
    rows = run.play(jobs)
    run.log(f"done in {time.time() - t0:.0f} s")
    return rows


def search(
    run,
    minutes=10,
    start=64,
    seeds=2,
    seed=0,
    test_top=8,
    test_seeds=3,
    baselines=("naive",),
    around=None,
    agent="calc",
):
    """Successive halving over random Calculator knobs on the train pool, then the best `test_top`
    variants, the default and the baselines on the test pool. `around`: start from these knobs and
    their neighbours (one or two knobs changed) instead of random ones - a local search."""
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    names = [s.name for s in run.train]
    rng.shuffle(names)
    deadline = time.time() + 60 * minutes * 0.85  # the rest of the time is for the test phase
    fits = max(8, int(25 * minutes))  # about what a first round on an eighth of the scenarios can play
    if start > fits:
        run.log(f"{minutes:g} min fit about {fits} variants in a first round, not {start}: starting with {fits}")
        start = fits
    space = space_for(agent)
    if around is not None:
        variants = [(agent, dict(around)), (agent, {})] + [
            (agent, mutate(rng, around, space)) for _ in range(start - 2)
        ]
    else:
        variants = [(agent, {})] + [(agent, sample(rng, space)) for _ in range(start - 1)]
    size, played = max(12, len(names) // 8), {}
    rows = run.play([(b, {}, n, k) for b in baselines for n in names for k in range(seeds)])
    rnd = 0
    while variants and time.time() < deadline:
        rnd += 1
        subset = names[:size]
        jobs = []
        for name, knobs in variants:
            have = played.setdefault(_key(name, knobs), set())
            jobs += [(name, knobs, n, k) for n in subset if n not in have for k in range(seeds)]
            have.update(subset)
        before = len(rows)
        rows += run.play(jobs, deadline)
        if rnd == 1 and len(rows) - before < len(jobs):
            run.inconclusive = True
            run.log("the first round did not finish in time: the ranking is inconclusive, give it more minutes")
        means = {}
        for r in rows:
            means.setdefault(_key(r["strategy"], r["knobs"]), []).append(r["score"])
        ranked = sorted(variants, key=lambda v: -statistics.mean(means.get(_key(*v), [0])))
        best = statistics.mean(means.get(_key(*ranked[0]), [0]))
        run.log(f"round {rnd}: {len(variants)} variants on {len(subset)} train scenarios, best {100 * best:.1f}")
        if size >= len(names):
            keep = ranked[: max(4, len(ranked) // 4)]
            variants = keep + [(agent, mutate(rng, keep[i % len(keep)][1], space)) for i in range(len(keep) * 3)]
        else:
            variants = ranked[: max(4, len(ranked) // 2)]
            size = min(len(names), size * 2)
    calc_rows = [r for r in rows if r["strategy"] == agent]
    stats = summarise(calc_rows, min_scenarios=len(names))
    top = sorted(stats.values(), key=lambda x: -x["mean"])[:test_top]
    if not top:  # nothing was played on every train scenario: take the widest-played ones
        top = sorted(summarise(calc_rows).values(), key=lambda x: (-x["scenarios"], -x["mean"]))[:test_top]
    cands = [(agent, t["knobs"]) for t in top] + [(b, {}) for b in baselines]
    if around is not None and not any(n == agent and k == around for n, k in cands):
        cands.append((agent, dict(around)))  # the champion is always scored on the test pool
    if not any(n == agent and not k for n, k in cands):
        cands.append((agent, {}))
    run.log(f"test phase: {len(cands)} strategies on {len(run.test)} test scenarios, {test_seeds} seeds")
    rows += run.play([(n, k, s.name, 100 + j) for n, k in cands for s in run.test for j in range(test_seeds)])
    run.log("search done")
    return rows


def mutate(rng, knobs, space=None):
    """A neighbour of a variant: one or two knobs re-drawn."""
    fresh = sample(rng, space or space_for("calc"))
    out = dict(knobs)
    for k in rng.sample(list(fresh), rng.randint(1, 2)):
        out[k] = fresh[k]
    return out


def _mean(xs):
    return statistics.mean(xs) if xs else math.nan

class Run:
    """A run folder with its scenario pools, a pool of workers and a progress log."""

    def __init__(self, out, opts, train, test, workers=None, log=print):
        self.out, self.opts, self.log_fn = Path(out), opts, log
        self.out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        self.progress = open(self.out / "progress.log", "a", encoding="utf-8", buffering=1)  # noqa: SIM115
        self.train, self.test = train, test
        for s in self.train:
            s.notes = "train"
        for s in self.test:
            s.notes = "test"
        path = self.out / "scenarios.json.gz"
        store.save(self.train + self.test, path)
        n_tw_train = sum(s.kind == "twin" for s in self.train)
        n_tw_test = sum(s.kind == "twin" for s in self.test)
        self.log(
            f"pools: train {len(self.train)} ({n_tw_train} twins), test {len(self.test)} ({n_tw_test} twins); "
            f"options {opts}"
        )
        self.pool = ProcessPoolExecutor(workers, initializer=_init, initargs=(str(path), opts))

    def log(self, text):
        line = f"{time.strftime('%H:%M:%S')} {text}"
        self.progress.write(line + "\n")
        self.log_fn(line)

    def play(self, jobs, deadline=None):
        """Rows for the jobs, in batches; stops early (keeping what is done) once past `deadline`."""
        rows = []
        for i in range(0, len(jobs), BATCH):
            if deadline and time.time() > deadline:
                self.log(f"time is up: {len(jobs) - i} negotiations of this round not played")
                break
            rows += list(self.pool.map(_play, jobs[i : i + BATCH], chunksize=8))
        return rows

    def close(self):
        self.pool.shutdown()
        self.progress.close()

"""Per-case playbooks: for each twin the knob set of the negotiator that scores best in the lab.

`python -m sellm.lab.playbooks base [--llm]` scores the champion (sellm.agent defaults) on every twin;
`... search P01 --minutes 10 [--llm]` searches the negotiator's knobs on one twin and its family.
"""

import argparse
import json
import random
import statistics
import time
from pathlib import Path

from arena_kit.cli import load_env
from arena_kit.data import DataPackage

from . import twins
from .spaces import NEGOTIATOR
from .tournament import Run, mutate

AGENT = "sellm.agent:make_agent"
ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]


def opts(llm, think=2.0):
    return dict(clock=True, wave_cap_s=480.0, think_s=think, vary=True, mode="parallel",
                supplier="llm" if llm else "engine", reader=None, no_cache=False)  # fmt: skip


def scenarios(names=None):
    tw = twins.load()
    return [s for s in tw if not names or s.name in names]


def score_table(rows):
    by = {}
    for r in rows:
        by.setdefault((r["scenario"], json.dumps(r["knobs"], sort_keys=True)), []).append(r["score"])
    return by


def main(argv=None):
    load_env(ROOT / ".env")
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("cmd", choices=["base", "search"])
    ap.add_argument("names", nargs="*")
    ap.add_argument("--llm", action="store_true")
    ap.add_argument("--seeds", type=int, default=6)
    ap.add_argument("--minutes", type=float, default=10)
    ap.add_argument("--knobs", default="{}")
    ap.add_argument("--out", default="")
    a = ap.parse_args(argv)
    sc = scenarios(a.names)
    out = a.out or str(ROOT / "runs" / "lab" / f"{time.strftime('%Y%m%d-%H%M')}-playbook-{a.cmd}")
    run = Run(out, opts(a.llm), sc, [], workers=8)
    try:
        if a.cmd == "base":
            knobs = json.loads(a.knobs)
            rows = run.play([(AGENT, knobs, s.name, k) for s in sc for k in range(a.seeds)])
            for (name, _), v in sorted(score_table(rows).items()):
                print(f"{name:6s} {statistics.mean(v):.3f}  (n={len(v)}, min {min(v):.2f})")
            print("mean", round(statistics.mean(r["score"] for r in rows), 3))
            print("llm_fail", sum(r.get("llm_fail", 0) for r in rows), "crash", sum(1 for r in rows if r.get("crash")))
        else:
            rng = random.Random(1)
            champ = json.loads(a.knobs)
            variants = [champ] + [mutate(rng, champ, NEGOTIATOR) for _ in range(60)]
            deadline = time.time() + 60 * a.minutes
            results = {}
            while time.time() < deadline and variants:
                rows = run.play([(AGENT, v, s.name, k) for v in variants for s in sc for k in range(a.seeds)], deadline)
                for (name, kj), v in score_table(rows).items():
                    results.setdefault(kj, []).extend(v)
                ranked = sorted(results.items(), key=lambda kv: -statistics.mean(kv[1]))
                print(f"best so far {statistics.mean(ranked[0][1]):.3f} {ranked[0][0]}", flush=True)
                top = [json.loads(k) for k, _ in ranked[:6]]
                variants = [mutate(rng, rng.choice(top), NEGOTIATOR) for _ in range(40)]
            ranked = sorted(results.items(), key=lambda kv: -statistics.mean(kv[1]))
            Path(out, "best.json").write_text(json.dumps(
                [{"mean": round(statistics.mean(v), 4), "n": len(v), "knobs": json.loads(k)} for k, v in ranked[:10]],
                indent=1))  # fmt: skip
            for k, v in ranked[:5]:
                print(f"{statistics.mean(v):.3f} n={len(v)} {k}")
    finally:
        run.close()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
EOF

"""Cross-test of the per-twin playbooks: every twin's best knobs on every twin (engine or LLM suppliers).
The diagonal says how much tuning gains; the off-diagonal how much of it is specific to that supplier."""

import json
import statistics
import sys
from pathlib import Path

from arena_kit.cli import load_env

from .playbooks import AGENT, ROOT, opts, scenarios
from .tournament import Run

NAMES = ["P01", "P02", "P03", "P04", "P05", "P07", "P08", "P10", "P11", "P18", "D01", "D02"]


def load_best(prefix="engine"):
    out = {}
    for n in NAMES:
        p = ROOT / "runs" / "lab" / "playbooks" / f"{prefix}-{n}" / "best.json"
        out[n] = json.loads(p.read_text())[0]["knobs"] if p.is_file() else {}
    return out


def main(llm=False, seeds=4):
    load_env(ROOT / ".env")
    sc = scenarios()
    best = load_best()
    books = {"champion": {}, **{f"pb-{n}": k for n, k in best.items()}}
    out = ROOT / "runs" / "lab" / "playbooks" / ("matrix-llm" if llm else "matrix-engine")
    run = Run(out, opts(llm), sc, [], workers=24 if llm else 8)
    try:
        jobs = [(AGENT, k, s.name, 500 + j) for k in books.values() for s in sc for j in range(seeds)]
        rows = run.play(jobs)
    finally:
        run.close()
    key = {json.dumps(k, sort_keys=True): n for n, k in books.items()}
    tab = {}
    for r in rows:
        tab.setdefault((key[json.dumps(r["knobs"], sort_keys=True)], r["scenario"]), []).append(r["score"])
    lines = ["book \\ twin  " + " ".join(f"{n:>5}" for n in NAMES) + "   mean"]
    for b in books:
        vals = [statistics.mean(tab[(b, n)]) for n in NAMES]
        lines.append(f"{b:12s} " + " ".join(f"{v:5.2f}" for v in vals) + f"  {statistics.mean(vals):.3f}")
    diag = statistics.mean(statistics.mean(tab[(f"pb-{n}", n)]) for n in NAMES)
    lines.append(f"diagonal (own book on own twin) {diag:.3f}; llm_fail {sum(r.get('llm_fail', 0) for r in rows)}; "
                 f"crash {sum(1 for r in rows if r.get('crash'))}")  # fmt: skip
    text = "\n".join(lines)
    (out / "matrix.txt").write_text(text + "\n")
    print(text)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main(llm="--llm" in sys.argv, seeds=int(next((a.split("=")[1] for a in sys.argv if a.startswith("--seeds=")), 4)))
EOF

"""Playbook per group of cases vs one merged playbook, scored on scenarios the search never saw.

`python -m sellm.lab.pb_groups --by type --minutes 3`: for every group (case type, or goal, or
archetype of the first supplier) a knob search on the group's generated training scenarios, then every
group book, the merged book and the champion on the group's held-out scenarios.
"""

import argparse
import json
import statistics
import time

from arena_kit.cli import load_env
from arena_kit.data import DataPackage

from . import tournament as T
from .playbooks import AGENT, ROOT, opts


def group_of(s, by):
    if by == "type":
        return s.case.get("type")
    if by == "goal":
        return s.case["buyer"].get("category_goal")
    return sorted({p.archetype for p in s.personas.values()})[0]


def main(argv=None):
    load_env(ROOT / ".env")
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--by", default="type", choices=["type", "goal", "archetype"])
    ap.add_argument("--minutes", type=float, default=3)
    ap.add_argument("--merged-minutes", type=float, default=10)
    ap.add_argument("--train", type=int, default=400)
    ap.add_argument("--test", type=int, default=200)
    ap.add_argument("--llm", action="store_true", help="the test phase with LLM suppliers")
    a = ap.parse_args(argv)
    pkg = DataPackage(ROOT / "data" / "package")
    pkg.lookup("")
    train, test = T.build_pools(a.train, 7, a.test, pkg)
    out = ROOT / "runs" / "lab" / "playbooks" / f"{time.strftime('%Y%m%d-%H%M')}-groups-{a.by}"
    out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    groups = sorted({group_of(s, a.by) for s in train} - {None})
    books = {}
    for g in ["ALL", *groups]:
        tr = train if g == "ALL" else [s for s in train if group_of(s, a.by) == g]
        te = test if g == "ALL" else [s for s in test if group_of(s, a.by) == g]
        if len(tr) < 12 or not te:
            print(f"{g}: {len(tr)} train / {len(te)} test scenarios: skipped", flush=True)
            continue
        run = T.Run(out / g, opts(False), tr, te, workers=8, log=lambda *_: None)
        try:
            rows = T.search(run, minutes=a.merged_minutes if g == "ALL" else a.minutes, start=48, seeds=2,
                            test_top=3, test_seeds=2, baselines=(), around=None, agent=AGENT)  # fmt: skip
        finally:
            run.close()
        stats = T.summarise([r for r in rows if r["pool"] == "train"], min_scenarios=len(tr) // 2)
        top = max(stats.values(), key=lambda x: x["mean"])
        books[g] = top["knobs"]
        print(f"{g}: {len(tr)} train, {len(te)} test; book (train {100 * top['mean']:.1f}) {json.dumps(top['knobs'])}", flush=True)
    (out / "books.json").write_text(json.dumps(books, indent=1))
    # held-out comparison: each scenario of the test pool, with its group's book, the merged book, the champion
    o = opts(a.llm)
    run = T.Run(out / "final", o, [], test, workers=24 if a.llm else 8, log=lambda *_: None)
    try:
        jobs, who = [], {}
        for s in test:
            g = group_of(s, a.by)
            for label, k in (("champion", {}), ("merged", books.get("ALL", {})), ("group", books.get(g, books.get("ALL", {})))):
                for j in range(3):
                    jobs.append((AGENT, k, s.name, 900 + j))
                    who[(json.dumps(k, sort_keys=True), s.name, 900 + j, label)] = g
        rows = run.play(jobs)
    finally:
        run.close()
    lab = {}
    for r in rows:
        k = json.dumps(r["knobs"], sort_keys=True)
        for label, bk in (("champion", {}), ("merged", books.get("ALL", {})), ("group", books.get(group_of(next(s for s in test if s.name == r["scenario"]), a.by), books.get("ALL", {})))):
            if k == json.dumps(bk, sort_keys=True):
                lab.setdefault(label, {}).setdefault(group_of(next(s for s in test if s.name == r["scenario"]), a.by), []).append(r["score"])
    lines = [f"held-out test ({'LLM' if a.llm else 'engine'} suppliers), by {a.by}", f"{'group':14s} " + " ".join(f"{l:>9}" for l in ('champion', 'merged', 'group'))]
    for g in groups:
        lines.append(f"{g:14s} " + " ".join(f"{statistics.mean(lab[l][g]):9.3f}" if g in lab.get(l, {}) else f"{'-':>9}" for l in ("champion", "merged", "group")))
    allv = {l: [x for v in lab[l].values() for x in v] for l in lab}
    lines.append(f"{'ALL':14s} " + " ".join(f"{statistics.mean(allv[l]):9.3f}" for l in ("champion", "merged", "group")))
    text = "\n".join(lines)
    (out / "report.txt").write_text(text + "\n")
    print(text)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
EOF

Der Stand ist gepusht (`038ed5d`). Die zufälligen Knob-Suchen und die Matrizen sind committet.

**Nicht gepusht**, mit Absicht:
- Der Ordner `runs/lab/playbooks/20261010-2158-groups-type/` und die `progress.log`-Dateien der Twin-Suchen. Der Gruppen-Lauf (nach Fall-Typ, mit zusammengefasstem Vergleichs-Buch) läuft noch im Hintergrund und schreibt dort hinein.
- Der leere Ordner `runs/lab/20261010-2132-playbook-base/`. Das war nur ein Testlauf.

Das Ergebnis des Gruppen-Laufs trage ich nach, sobald er fertig ist.

Offen ist deine Frage von eben: Die systematische Reihe habe ich noch nicht gebaut. Gemeint war: jeden Persönlichkeitswert einzeln hochdrehen (Überzeugung, Aggressivität, Zahlungsziel 1 gegen 90 Tage) und danach die Kombinationen testen, jeweils für P01, P02 und so weiter. Das wäre der nächste Schritt. Dafür brauche ich diese Werte als echte Regler im Negotiator-Aufsatz.

Bisher habe ich nur die Regler gedreht, die Jonathans Negotiator schon hat (`DEFAULTS` in `sellm/negotiator.py`). Das ist grob, und mit Überzeugung oder Aggressivität hat es wenig zu tun.

**Die vorhandenen Regler:**

| Regler | Was er tut | Hängt mit deiner Idee zusammen als |
|---|---|---|
| `open_below` | wie weit unter unserer Schätzung wir die erste Forderung setzen | Aggressivität |
| `pace` | welchen Anteil unserer Schritte der Lieferant erwartungsgemäß zurückgibt, daraus folgt unsere Schrittgröße | Aggressivität / Tempo |
| `horizon` | in wie vielen Nachrichten sich die Preise treffen sollen | Geduld |
| `keep_below` | wie nah wir ans Lieferantenangebot herangehen, bevor er den letzten Schritt macht | Härte |
| `floor_share` | wo wir seine Untergrenze als Anteil seines Eröffnungspreises vermuten | Annahme, wie viel noch drin ist |
| `rate_guess` | Annahme zu seinen Finanzierungskosten | Gewicht von Zahlungstausch |
| `claims` | `none` oder `bank`: ein geprüftes Datenargument pro Mail | Überzeugung (an/aus) |
| `max_holds` | wie oft wir bei RFQ-Fäden warten | Ablauf |
| `levers` | erste Forderung: unser günstigstes Paket oder seine Bedingungen mit gedecktem Bedarf | Struktur |
| `dossier` | liest seine Finanzlage aus Omars Dossier | Einsicht |

`rounds_to_floor` steht im Such-Raum, aber nicht in `DEFAULTS`. Er hat vermutlich keine Wirkung. Das prüfe ich zuerst.

**Die Regler, die du meinst, gibt es noch nicht.** Ich würde sie in einer Unterklasse in meiner eigenen Datei bauen, damit Jonathans Datei unberührt bleibt:
- **Zahlungsziel:** Stufen 14, 30, 60, 90 Tage als feste Forderung. Heute entscheidet das der Rechner nach der Finanzlage des Lieferanten.
- **Überzeugung:** Anzahl Argumente pro Mail (0 bis 3), welche Sorte zuerst (Kündigungsfrist, Index, Kosten, Forecast, Scorecard, Wertschätzung) und ob wir sie sofort oder erst nach der ersten Antwort bringen.
- **Ton:** warm, neutral oder bestimmt.
- **Struktur:** Vertragslaufzeit lang oder kurz, Startdatum früh oder spät, Index-Klausel ja oder nein, Anzahl Term Sheets (1 bis 3).
- **Abschluss:** wie früh wir annehmen und ob wir die Alternative des Lieferanten nehmen.

**Das Vorgehen, wie du es beschrieben hast:**
1. Für jeden Fall (P01 bis P18, D01, D02) jeden Regler einzeln durchfahren: niedrig, mittel, hoch. Alle anderen bleiben auf Standard.
2. Pro Fall die Regler behalten, die wirklich etwas bewegen.
3. Danach die Kombinationen der besten Regler testen, auch hier pro Fall.
4. Das Ergebnis mit LLM-Lieferanten bestätigen, dann online mit höchstens 25 Sessions.

"""Dial sweeps on one twin: every dial alone at each level (all others at their defaults), then the
best levels combined. Paired seeds: every level is played on the same twin family members.

    python -m sellm.lab.dial_sweep P02 [--llm] [--seeds 8] [--phase one|combo|both]
"""

import argparse
import itertools
import json
import statistics
import time

from arena_kit.cli import load_env

from .playbooks import ROOT, opts, scenarios
from .tournament import Run

AGENT = "sellm.lab.dials:DialNegotiator"
LEVELS = {
    "pay_days": [30, 60, 90],
    "idx": ["none", "db0", "db3", "db5"],
    "open_below": [0.02, 0.06, 0.10, 0.15],
    "pace": [0.3, 0.5, 0.8, 1.0],
    "horizon": [3, 4, 5, 6],
    "keep_below": [0.0, 0.006, 0.02],
    "floor_share": [0.88, 0.92, 0.96, 0.98],
    "n_args": [0, 1, 2, 3],
    "arg_first": [0, 1],
    "arg_order": ["history", "delivery", "notice", "forecast", "quality"],
    "tone": ["warm", "firm"],
}


def play(run, books, names, seeds):
    jobs = [(AGENT, k, n, 700 + j) for k in books for n in names for j in range(seeds)]
    rows = run.play(jobs)
    out = {}
    for r in rows:
        out.setdefault(json.dumps(r["knobs"], sort_keys=True), {})[(r["scenario"], r["seed"])] = r["score"]
    return out, rows


def stats(cell, base):
    keys = sorted(set(cell) & set(base))
    d = [cell[k] - base[k] for k in keys]
    m = statistics.mean(cell[k] for k in keys)
    se = statistics.stdev(d) / len(d) ** 0.5 if len(d) > 1 else 0.0
    return m, statistics.mean(d), se


def main():
    load_env(ROOT / ".env")
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("case")
    ap.add_argument("--llm", action="store_true")
    ap.add_argument("--seeds", type=int, default=8)
    ap.add_argument("--phase", default="both", choices=["one", "combo", "both"])
    ap.add_argument("--top", type=int, default=4, help="dials whose best level goes into the combinations")
    a = ap.parse_args()
    sc = scenarios([a.case])
    out = ROOT / "runs" / "lab" / "playbooks" / f"{time.strftime('%Y%m%d-%H%M')}-dials-{a.case}-{'llm' if a.llm else 'engine'}"
    run = Run(out, opts(a.llm), sc, [], workers=24 if a.llm else 8, log=lambda *_: None)
    lines = []
    try:
        names = [a.case]
        base_books = [{}]
        books = base_books + [{d: v} for d, vs in LEVELS.items() for v in vs]
        cells, rows = play(run, books, names, a.seeds)
        base = cells["{}"]
        lines.append(f"{a.case} one dial at a time ({'LLM' if a.llm else 'engine'} suppliers, {a.seeds} paired seeds); baseline {statistics.mean(base.values()):.3f}")
        best = {}
        for d, vs in LEVELS.items():
            res = []
            for v in vs:
                m, delta, se = stats(cells[json.dumps({d: v}, sort_keys=True)], base)
                res.append((v, m, delta, se))
            lines.append(f"  {d:12s} " + "  ".join(f"{v}:{m:.3f}({delta:+.3f}±{se:.3f})" for v, m, delta, se in res))
            top = max(res, key=lambda r: r[1])
            if top[2] > 1.5 * top[3] and top[2] > 0.005:
                best[d] = (top[0], top[2])
        lines.append("  levels clearly above the baseline: " + json.dumps({d: v[0] for d, v in best.items()}))
        if a.phase != "one" and best:
            chosen = sorted(best, key=lambda d: -best[d][1])[: a.top]
            alt = {d: [best[d][0], *[v for v in LEVELS[d] if v != best[d][0]][:0]] for d in chosen}
            combos = []
            for r in range(1, len(chosen) + 1):
                for sub in itertools.combinations(chosen, r):
                    combos.append({d: best[d][0] for d in sub})
            cells2, rows2 = play(run, combos, names, a.seeds)
            lines.append("combinations of the best levels:")
            res = sorted(((stats(cells2[json.dumps(c, sort_keys=True)], base), c) for c in combos), key=lambda x: -x[0][0])
            for (m, delta, se), c in res[:8]:
                lines.append(f"  {m:.3f} ({delta:+.3f}±{se:.3f})  {json.dumps(c)}")
            (out / "best.json").write_text(json.dumps([{"mean": round(m, 4), "knobs": c} for (m, _, _), c in res[:8]], indent=1))
        lines.append(f"llm_fail {sum(r.get('llm_fail', 0) for r in rows)}  crash {sum(1 for r in rows if r.get('crash'))}")
    finally:
        run.close()
    text = "\n".join(lines)
    (out / "report.txt").write_text(text + "\n")
    print(text)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
EOF

Die fünf echten P02-Tests brachten keinen Gewinn: Alle Varianten landeten bei 0.48 bis 0.53, genau auf dem Niveau des bisherigen Negotiators (0.52 bis 0.53).

| Variante | Score | Preis (bei 90 Tagen) |
|---|---|---|
| a1: Lab-beste Härte (`horizon` 3, `keep_below` 0, `pace` 0.3) | 0.527 | 371.70 |
| a2: a1 plus 2 Argumente pro Mail | 0.510 | 371.85 |
| a3: a1 plus 3 Argumente, Preisverlauf und Forecast zuerst | **0.531** | 371.66 |
| a4: a1 plus 2 Argumente plus Verständnis-Satz | 0.521 | 371.75 |
| a5: normale Härte plus 2 Argumente | 0.482 | 372.10 |

Alle fünf enden innerhalb von 0.45 € voneinander. Die im Lab vorhergesagten +0.055 für die härtere Linie sind also nicht eingetreten. Mehr Argumente oder ein wärmerer Ton haben den Preis auch nicht bewegt. Nordmark scheint bei etwa 371.7 € (bei 90 Tagen) seine Grenze zu haben, `C_best` liegt bei etwa 368 €.

**Du hast recht, das Lab hat hier nichts gebracht.** Es sagt für P02 nur noch etwas aus, wenn echte Lieferanten es bestätigen.

**Auffällig:** In a2, a4 und a5 hat die Arena eine Behauptung als `contradicted` gewertet. Dort standen in einer Mail die Lieferquote (`sc`) und eine Reklamation (`qn`) zusammen. Vermutlich liest die Arena die Lieferquote dann als Qualitätswert. In a1 und a3 passierte das nicht. Ob es Preis kostet, habe ich nicht geprüft.

Verbraucht habe ich 5 Sessions, übrig sind 321 von 450. Alles ist geloggt und gepusht (`5e01d45`). Mein Lab-Refit (`twins.json`) liegt weiter unveröffentlicht.
